post_text:
CUATRECASAS SELLS ‘SPECIAL SITUATIONS’.

HERE IS ONE IT SHOULD EXPLAIN.

Cuatrecasas publicly markets expertise in restructuring, insolvency, NPLs, distressed debt, credit bidding, loan-to-own and enforcement.

So why, in our documented Sun Park matter, does the fee-recovery path appear to jump straight to Step 4?

1. Demand payment from the mandating UK client, Aweswell? Not evidenced in the record presently located.

2. Seek payment through LPB’s Concurso 36/2012? Not evidenced as the payment route used.

3. Seek payment through the operating hotel/recovery structure? Not evidenced in the record presently located.

4. Execute against Matkator? YES.

The current remate concerns one property only: finca registral 8,584. But the executed debtor is Matkator, S.L. That distinction matters. Subject to the execution order, balance, proportionality and attachability rules, the exposure is not conceptually limited to one apartment: other legally attachable Matkator assets or patrimonial rights may potentially matter.

And Matkator is the wholly owned subsidiary of Aweswell — the UK client whose wider hotel recovery Cuatrecasas had been retained to assist.

That is why we call this MANDATE INVERSION.

The pagarés were documented in 2018 as covering pending invoices and incurred costs. In 2019 Cuatrecasas itself identified Matkator’s free assets as potential rescue-financing collateral.

So the question is not simply whether fees could be collected. It is: WHY DID FEE-DERIVED INSTRUMENTS BECOME THE ROUTE INTO THE SAME PATRIMONIAL BASE THE MANDATE WAS SUPPOSED TO HELP PROTECT, FINANCE OR RECOVER?

And why Step 4 first?

If Steps 1–3 happened, show the documents.

Full evidence-led reconstruction: https://sbu001monterecco.github.io/por-derecho/en/cuatrecasas-sun-park/

Facts, inferences and allegations remain separate.

#Cuatrecasas #SpecialSituations #Insolvency #NPL #ProfessionalResponsibility #SunPark
